name: נגזרת של secⁿ(x) – רמז לכתוב כ-1/cos (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Find the following derivative:

\( \displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}({{CT:1}}) = \) [[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]

Hint: write \({{CT:2}}\) as \(1/{{CT:3}}\)
generalfeedback:
Outline: Write the secant as a reciprocal, then use the chain rule for the power and the quotient rule for the reciprocal.
Step 1 — Rewriting the function
Since \({{CT:2}}=\frac{1}{{CT:3}}\), \({{CT:1}}=\frac{1}{{CT:3}}^{{CT:4}}\)
Step 2 — The chain rule and the quotient rule
So, using the chain rule and the quotient rule,
The chain rule: \( \frac{d}{dx}f(g(x))=f'(g(x))\,g'(x) \)
The quotient rule: \( \frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{u}{v}\right)=\frac{u'v-uv'}{v^2} \)

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}({{CT:1}}) &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[\left(\frac{1}{{CT:3}}\right)^{{CT:4}}\right] \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:4}}\left[\frac{1}{{CT:3}}\right]^{({{CT:4}}-1)}\cdot \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[\frac{1}{{CT:3}}\right] \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{{CT:4}}{{{CT:3}}^{{CT:5}}}\cdot \frac{\frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}[1]\cdot {{CT:3}}-1\cdot \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}[{{CT:3}}]}{{{CT:3}}^2} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:6}}\cdot \frac{0-{{CT:7}}}{{CT:8}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:9}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:10}} \end{array} \]
